newsitem.title: GREECE: Privatisation to fuel Athens bourse growth - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Privatisation to fuel Athens bourse growth - Salomon.

text.p: The Athens stock exchange will soar on the privatisation of state companies from the financial and infrastruture sectors, the managing director of corporate finance at Salomon Brothers said on Tuesday.
"I can assure you the Athens stock exchange will experience a growth in future years which will astonish most of us," Jean Grall told an economic conference organised by the Economist.

Greece will find it easier to fulfil the Maastricht criteria if it engages in a more active management of its state assets by using methods such as securitisation, which converts assets into tradeable securities, he said.

"This is where privatisation meets securitisation: A number of assets of the state, not only companies but real estate and securities, can be taken "off the books" of the country so to speak, along with the corresponding debt," said Grall.
The financial and infrastruture sectors should be the prime candidates for privatisation, he added.

"Experts should focus on...the financial institutions sector, which is ripe for restructuring, and the infrastructure sector, which after some financial and legislative preparation could become a source of substantial stock exchange flotations," said Grall.

He added that there was scope for further concentration and increased efficiency in the financial sector and noted that the top five Portuguese banks control 82 percent of the country's banking sector as opposed to 62 percent in Greece.

The Public Power Corporation (DEH) was one of the most valuable assets of the state, with the new Athens airport company and some regional airports, port authorites and motorway concession companies also good candidates for flotation, he added. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Intercontinental Newsroom +301 9206370
